questions.question: Define a scraped surface heat exchanger.
questions.solution_html:
• A scraped surface heat exchanger (SSHE) is a type of heat exchanger designed for viscous
  • sticky, or heat-sensitive food products. It uses rotating blades to continuously scrape the inner
  • surface of the heat exchanger, preventing fouling and ensuring uniform heat transfer.
questions.final_answer: surface of the heat exchanger, preventing fouling and ensuring uniform heat transfer

questions.question: What are the limitations of water distillation?
questions.solution_html:
•  High energy consumption due to vaporization, Scaling and corrosion of equipment.
  •  Not suitable for heat-sensitive materials, Low throughput compared to membrane
  • techniques.

questions.question: Why is radiation dominant in high-temperature food processes like broiling?
questions.solution_html:
• At high temperatures, heat transfer occurs mainly through electromagnetic radiation rather
  • than conduction or convection because radiant energy can travel directly through air and
  • rapidly heat the food surface.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is regeneration efficiency in plate heat exchangers?
questions.solution_html:
• Regeneration efficiency is the ratio of heat recovered from the outgoing (hot) product to the
  • total heat required to heat the incoming product.

questions.question: Discuss how direct contact steam injection improves heating efficiency.
questions.solution_html:
•  Steam directly contacts the product, condensing and transferring latent heat instantly.
  •  Minimizes heat loss and provides rapid temperature rise ,Ideal for liquid foods (soups
  • sauces, milk),Reduces fouling since no heat surface contact.However, steam
  • condensate dilutes the product slightly.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Rank the applications of microfiltration in food processing.
questions.solution_html:
• Rank the applications of microfiltration in food processing.
  • Clarification of fruit juices and wines, Removal of bacteria from milk and beer, Separation of
  • fat globules from whey.Pre-treatment for ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis.
  • Microfiltration enhances microbial safety and product clarity without thermal degradation.
questions.final_answer: Microfiltration enhances microbial safety and product clarity without thermal degradation
